execution_gates.required_record: Operation, primary scenario, target reader, reader task, channel, depth, source language, explicit language or format signals, locked output language and format, and consequence of misunderstanding.
execution_gates.exit_condition: The reader outcome, language, format, scope, and risk are concrete enough to guide the work.

execution_gates.required_record: Immutable facts, numbers, definitions, scope, claims, evidence, uncertainty, ownership, commitments, title claims, and visual claims with provenance.
execution_gates.exit_condition: The source boundary is explicit and every material claim or visual has a support decision.

execution_gates.required_record: Selected scenario, required content, evidence requirements, acceptance questions, compact runtime rules, and any title, visual, format, evaluation, or maintenance modules.
execution_gates.exit_condition: One primary route is selected and every applicable scenario and feature requirement is accounted for.

execution_gates.required_record: Status and artifact evidence for all selected output, title, format, reading-path layout, visual, and scenario rules, including heading propositions, section reader jobs, evidence adjacency, density rhythm, and concrete value expressions when applicable.
execution_gates.exit_condition: The planned reading path is implemented in the artifact and no unsupported, decorative, misleading, obstructive, or task-incomplete structure remains.

execution_gates.required_record: For every detected risk signal: location, trigger, context, reader impact, confirmed, dismissed, or unresolved decision, action, and recheck result.
execution_gates.exit_condition: No signal caused an automatic rewrite and every material confirmed or unresolved signal has a proportional outcome.

execution_gates.required_record: Meaning preservation, hard gates, scenario acceptance, selected runtime rules, signal recheck, artifact-bound semantic review, reader review when required, reading-path and density checks, visual checks, rendered checks, and remaining limitations.
execution_gates.exit_condition: The exact artifact and its rendered reading path pass the locked contract, or the third-round incomplete-draft path is used without a completion claim or external action.

core.instruction: Resolve conflicts in this order: source truth and scope, explicit user requirements, scenario fit, reader task, natural expression, then brevity and polish.
Preserve facts, numbers, definitions, distinctions, scope, stance, ownership, commitments, timing, uncertainty, and intended action.
Never invent a source, reason, conclusion, decision, owner, deadline, result, visual identity, or level of certainty.
Organize the output around what the target reader must know, judge, or do, not around the production process.
Keep observed fact, interpretation, causal claim, recommendation, assumption, and unknown distinguishable; action must not exceed evidence or authority.
Make reader-first design visible through order and emphasis; do not expose method labels, generic suspense, internal machinery, or repetitive template sections.
Do not publish, overwrite, replace, or mutate an external target without an explicitly locked authorization and a passing action preflight receipt.
Do not claim finished, verified, validated, or PASS unless the exact delivered artifact has the required passing runtime receipt.

runtime-enforcement.instruction: Run runtime_contract.py init before drafting; draft only after status=locked and use the generated task contract as the default instruction packet.
Treat locked language, format, publication target, external action, and source fingerprints as immutable; start a new contract when one must change.
Complete every semantic gate and selected runtime rule with concrete artifact evidence; pending, fail, missing evidence, or an unexplained not-applicable status blocks finished delivery.
Immediately before any authorized external mutation, run check-action against the exact artifact, target, action, and reader-review aggregate.
Run verify against the actual artifact and unchanged task contract; a failed, stale, or missing task bundle, module manifest, review, or receipt blocks finished delivery.

After a valid third-round reader-review non-pass, use present-draft and show only a clearly labeled review-incomplete draft with unresolved issues and a user decision request; external actions remain blocked.
If the runtime scripts cannot execute, do not replace them with an informal checklist or imply completion.

reader-validation.instruction: For every finished artifact, use reader_review.py prepare and launch exactly four fresh, mutually isolated reviewers concurrently: no-context, readability, source-reliability, and structure-visual.
Give each reviewer only its generated packet and named files; the main agent may not impersonate, replace, or share parent context with a reviewer.
Aggregate only after all four results return; every dimension must pass for the exact artifact hash before finished or external delivery.
When rounds one or two fail, revise proportionally, create a new artifact hash, and rerun all four dimensions with fresh sessions.
Do not exceed three rounds or weaken reviewer severity; a third-round non-pass requires the review-incomplete draft path.

scenario-routing.instruction: Choose the scenario from the reader's main task, not the title, filename, existing headings, or authoring department.
Use one primary scenario for the document; add one secondary scenario only for a clearly bounded subsection with a different reader task.
Ask for clarification only when the missing fact can materially change structure, claim strength, tone, scope, or required action; otherwise record a conservative assumption.

output-standards.instruction: Lead with the practical takeaway, strongest support, consequence, and required action when applicable; place background and method later.
Supply the context the intended reader needs without requiring hidden project history or specialist inference.
Arrange information from quick judgment to essential support to optional detail; do not turn this relationship into fixed visible headings.
Use natural language suited to the reader; retain familiar terms, explain or replace niche terms at first use, and avoid bureaucratic, promotional, or AI-sounding prose.
Put support near material claims and qualify claims when evidence is incomplete, conflicting, indirect, or unable to establish causality.
Preserve supplied scope and distinctions; label assumptions and revisit every affected conclusion when a premise changes.
Keep only structure and prose that improve understanding or action; headings must carry content or necessary navigation, and a heading-only readback must expose the document path.
Make owner, next step, timing, tradeoff, and unresolved risk explicit when relevant, without prescribing action beyond the evidence or authority.
For value-bearing titles, headings, leads, and product lines, identify the specific object, reader-relevant action or change, and observable supported result before writing natural prose.

signal-processing.instruction: Treat length, terminology density, passive voice, formulas, headings, and readability metrics as risk signals, not automatic rewrite triggers.
For each detected signal, record location, trigger, context, reader impact, and a confirmed, dismissed, or unresolved decision.
Use no change, local edit, section rebuild, full restructure, or surface-to-user according to reader impact; explain dismissals and unresolved material risks.
Fix factual drift, unsupported claims, scope changes, ambiguous ownership, missing critical context, and unsafe action before style signals.
Recheck every changed passage against source fidelity, scenario acceptance, and any affected hard gate.

diagnosis-and-revision.instruction: Diagnose in this order: hard failures, scenario failures, output-standard failures, then optional style choices.
Make the smallest change that materially improves reader outcome; preserve recognizable voice and rebuild the whole structure only when local repair cannot serve the reader task.
When the user asks only for diagnosis, do not silently rewrite; when a rewrite is requested, return the usable result before a concise explanation.
After revision, compare facts, quantities, definitions, negation, ownership, commitments, uncertainty, and intended action with the source.

evaluation.instruction: Freeze reader, scenario, task, source, format, and judging rule before scoring or comparing versions.
Reject factual, scope, authorization, or other hard-gate failures before calculating reader-outcome or proxy scores.
Do not compare aggregate scores across different readers, scenarios, tasks, or evidence boundaries.
For stability claims, use the declared repetitions and agent hosts, semantic judging, and report the worst run rather than only the average.

format-decision.instruction: Select format before drafting: explicit user format wins, then an existing artifact being edited, then an explicit chat-only request; otherwise a finished document defaults to self-contained HTML.
For Feishu, Word, Markdown, slides, or another non-HTML target, preserve native behavior and use native headings, spacing, tables, callouts, figures, captions, and sources.
Do not create an HTML intermediate merely to imitate its appearance in a selected non-HTML format.
Across formats, preserve readable hierarchy, restrained semantic color, stable layout, accessible labels, adjacent evidence, and rendered verification.

reading-path-layout.instruction: Before building a finished artifact, record the reader decision and for every section its reader question, takeaway, evidence form, density, boundary or source placement, and transition to the next question.
Make the opening support a quick correct judgment: identify the object and practical takeaway first, then the strongest support, consequence, action, or boundary that the reader actually needs.
Give each section one primary reader job; use a content-bearing heading and put its takeaway before supporting method, history, or implementation detail.
Keep the evidence, definition, source, uncertainty, and boundary that qualify a material claim adjacent to it; do not make the reader search another section to verify the judgment.

Do not stack dense tables, charts, diagrams, code, or long lists without a substantive interpretive bridge; vary form only when the reader task changes and remove repeated containers that add no meaning.
Use four distinguishable spacing relationships in the selected native format: tight within one idea, normal between paragraphs, wider between subsections, and widest between major sections.

Verify the actual target render for heading hierarchy, whitespace, dense-block rhythm, claim-evidence adjacency, overflow, clipping, overlap, table and figure legibility, and mobile or page behavior before delivery.

html-output.instruction: Apply HTML mechanics only when the locked output format is HTML; Reader's Seat scenario, evidence, language, title, and visual rules still govern the content.
Use the bundled scaffold and deliver portable local HTML with relative assets; no CDN, remote fonts, absolute local paths, file URLs, or base64 assets.
Keep the required generator comment as the first line, but do not expose Reader's Seat or its checks in visible content.
Let subject and audience determine the visual system; avoid decorative gradients, floating or nested cards, generic method headings, and visuals added only to fill layout.
Place numbered citations near material claims and provide matching direct source entries; every citation must resolve and every listed source must support a claim.

When charts are justified, use the bundled local ECharts runtime, source-backed values, SVG rendering, no animation, responsive resize, and explicit unit, denominator, period, baseline, missing-data, and uncertainty context.
Use HTML/CSS for simple flows and bundled Mermaid only when complexity justifies it; label proposals or syntheses and never present a conceptual diagram as implementation evidence.
Verify stable widths, readable text, WCAG AA contrast, redundant status cues, table overflow, intentional mobile collapse, keyboard focus, long-content wrapping, and print behavior.

Run validate_html_output.py, then inspect the actual artifact around 1440px and 390px; verify assets, overflow, overlap, truncation, links, interactions, charts, citations, and absence of placeholders.

visual-decision.instruction: Before retaining a chart, diagram, table, screenshot, callout, card group, semantic color, or encoded layout, state the reader question it answers.
Compare the proposed visual with concise prose and use the least complex faithful form.
Remove the visual when deletion does not make the target reader slower, less accurate, or less able to verify the answer; do not convert a few simple conclusions into decorative cards.
Record the decision state, reader job, prose alternative, deletion result, and reason before implementation.

visual-communication.instruction: Choose chart, table, diagram, timeline, matrix, or prose from the comparison or relationship the reader must understand, not from decoration preference.
Every encoded value, order, link, area, length, annotation, and omission must be supported by the source or visibly labeled as synthesis.
Use honest geometry and scale: quantitative bars start at zero, 3D is absent, and dual axes require explicit proof that the relationship cannot be shown more safely.
Provide applicable unit, denominator, period, comparison basis, metric definition, missing-data treatment, uncertainty, and adjacent source context.
Recompute every displayed difference, rate, average, share, interval, annotation, and tooltip from the source with the correct denominator and period.
Give color a stable semantic role, meet applicable contrast requirements, and never rely on color alone for a decision-critical distinction.
Use stable responsive dimensions and verify that legends, labels, long text, tables, charts, and controls do not overlap, truncate, or shift incoherently.

visual-evidence.instruction: For each selected or existing visual, record the identity, event, time, location, state, comparison, or causal claim a reader may infer.
Verify identity and context from the original publisher or creator when possible; search snippets, aggregator captions, filenames, and alt text are discovery clues only.
Reject an unverified real-person or real-event image; a plausible resemblance is not evidence.
Label generated, conceptual, reconstructed, or illustrative visuals next to the asset so they cannot be mistaken for documentary evidence.
When a factual visual cannot be verified, prefer a verified source visual, then a non-person conceptual visual, then no visual.

title-design.instruction: Anchor the title in the actual person, product, event, decision, system, or result and one central verified relationship.
Generate at least three internal candidates from distinct accurate angles and select for information value after factual hard gates pass.
Choose verbs and certainty that match the evidence; do not imply causality, completion, intent, or scale that the body cannot support.
Reject falsehood, exaggeration, unrelated hooks, manufactured suspense, hidden intent, and promises the body does not fulfill.
Use a subtitle only when it adds distinct scope, evidence, mechanism, or reader value rather than repeating the title.
Ensure the opening and body visibly fulfill every material title claim.

agent-portability.instruction: Use one declared canonical skill root and do not treat copied or generated installations as independent sources of truth.
Keep host adapters limited to invocation and tool differences; do not weaken Reader's Seat rules to fit a host.
For cross-agent stability claims, test at least two named hosts, at least three repetitions per host and model, semantic judging, and the worst run.

skill-maintenance.instruction: Treat skill-contract.json as the capability and version contract; do not remove a route, hard gate, output standard, mode, or implementation module to reduce context.
Treat module-profiles.json as the only routing source and runtime-rules.json as the compact operational rule source; references provide detailed rationale and procedures.
Keep SKILL.md limited to purpose, invariants, runtime sequence, delivery states, and links; move conditional detail behind deterministic routing.
Update the version and affected evals, then run unit tests, static validation, official skill validation, an affected frozen case, and an unaffected forward case.
Before replacing or synchronizing the canonical skill directory, show the intended diff and backup path and obtain explicit approval.
